What's So Great About Frame Rate?

The entire article seems to be based on "how many frames the eye can see", which is the wrong premise and can not yield a useful conclusion. The idea behind a high frame rate is the goal of a low latency. A low latency is not detected by your eyes or your visual system but by the part of your brain that coordinates senses with motorics. The threshold varies from brain to brain and you can train to be more sensitive in that area. Someone who has been playing Quake 3 or UT2k4 for years against skillful players will with utmost certainty notice a difference between 40 and 60 fps, especially if it fluctuates, because the result is that the latency from perceived hand movement to photons reaching the eye with confirmation of said movement will vary between 16.6 to 30 milliseconds. If your brain is trained to anticipate a constant latency of around 40 milliseconds because you have mostly been playing console games (which are often capped to 30 fps aka 33 ms render time per frame) with gamepads, then you will have trouble detecting the difference. This disparity is exactly why an absolute statement such as this article seems to seek is bogus and must not be valued.

The key is latency. The brain detects latency in coordination from hand to eye. Perception is relative.
